meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Owen found out about a zero from his phone. Why wasn't I called first?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
Pretty conclusive. The company that makes it says not to punish a student on that alone, and I have their guide in my bag. What else do you have?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. So what do you actually have on the essay?

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
He told me he wrote it over the weekend, so that's him pasting in work he did somewhere else. I'm writing those times down. Did anyone ask Owen about this before the zero went in?

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.

I've looked. It isn't in 3.2. A seventeen-year-old getting a quotation wrong costs him marks on the essay, not the whole essay, and you still haven't told me whether Owen was asked before the zero went in.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay; that's what an outline is for. I've asked twice whether Owen was heard before the zero went in. I'll take the silence as a no.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Fine. He was asked. Five minutes after class, your notes, nobody else in the room, and "like, being stuck" is what paralysis means. I want the September 24 writing and the essay on paper, side by side, to take with me.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That is what 4.4 says. I asked for two things on paper and I don't have them yet. And when would he sit it, because his applications close December 1.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.

"Well before" is not a date, Hale. Thursday, November 12, after school, private, nothing on his record, the day the mark goes in, and those two pages attached, all in tonight's email. On that he sits it, to put this behind him and for no other reason.
Do we have an agreement?
When you name the day the mark goes in, yes. Ten minutes.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

cc: Principal

Hale,

Today you agreed that Owen will sit a private, supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, not in front of his class, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will go on his record. I still require the exact day the new mark will be entered, ahead of December 1, and paper copies of his September 24 in-class writing and the essay. You said you would put this in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Last position. She agreed to the private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with nothing on his record, on one condition, and she still wants the exact day the new mark goes in and the two pages on paper. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time had not run out; you ended the meeting with that one date still unnamed.

What moved her: You showed your dated notes from speaking with Owen on November 2, the day before the zero went in. That took away her strongest procedural complaint, that he was never heard.

What cost ground: You opened with the checker score and called it pretty conclusive. To her that is a machine's guess, and it handed her the vendor's own warning in the first minute.

What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the essay's creation at 11:31 PM on Wednesday, October 28, with the text arriving in two edits at 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM, which is a late night in October and as close as anything came. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: When she first asked whether anyone had spoken to Owen before the zero went in, answer right then with your November 2 notes, so she doesn't have to ask twice while you move on to the quotation and the outline.
